summary: Couch Investor breaks down Bill Ackman's Pershing Square portfolio after six new positions were disclosed, alongside the firm's existing holdings. The six additions — Visa, Mastercard, Netflix, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange and Alcon — all fit Ackman's classic template: simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with strong moats, minimal leverage, 15-20%+ annual EPS growth, bought below intrinsic value, at 17-24x next-twelve-months earnings with 15-19% estimated 3-5 year EPS compound growth. He recaps Pershing's thesis for each: Visa and Mastercard derated on overblown stablecoin and AI-agent fears; Netflix a re-entry after a ~50% drawdown, with content spend barely up since 2021 while margins expanded from 21% to 31.5%; S&P Global an AI-fear selloff re-entry at 19x forward PE; Intercontinental Exchange hit by perpetual-futures fears; Alcon a margin-expansion story with an underappreciated FDA call option. He also reviews existing holdings — Uber (UBER, HOLD), where he agrees valuation is disconnected from ~35% earnings growth; Meta (META, HOLD), pressured by heavy AI capex but with ad growth at its fastest pace since 2021 and 20%+ expected earnings growth; plus Microsoft, Brookfield, Restaurant Brands, Amazon and Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac. The Howard Hughes 'modern-day Berkshire' insurance-compounding thesis and the new Pershing Square Ventures evergreen private-markets vehicle are also covered. His takeaway: Ackman is buying durable compounders positioned to beat the S&P for years, and he himself owns Meta, Google, Amazon, Uber and Netflix.
title: Bill Ackman Just Deployed $5B Into These 6 Stocks
